What Is Palestine? Palestine is a historical term for a region that has encompassed many territories — originally named by the Romans in 135 AD, when they renamed Judea in an attempt to sever the Jewish connection to the land. Across the centuries, the land was ruled by empire after empire, yet no sovereign country called Palestine ever existed. It began as a name meant to erase a people — and the question today is whether it's still being used to do exactly that. The last episode of "What Is" Season 1 is this Thursday at 11am ET.

Sad🇵🇸💔|| Palestine, officially known as the State of Palestine, is a country in the Middle East located along the eastern Mediterranean. It consists of the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip. Palestine is a land of immense historical, cultural, and religious importance, with a history stretching back thousands of years. Palestine is home to some of the world’s most historically significant cities and sites. Jerusalem is one of the holiest cities in the world and is sacred to Muslims, Christians, and Jews. Bethlehem is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Jesus Christ, while Jericho is among the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities. Modern Palestinian national identity developed over many generations and became especially prominent during the 19th and 20th centuries. The Palestinian Declaration of Independence was proclaimed in 1988, and in 2012 the United Nations granted Palestine non-member observer State status. Today, most UN member states recognize the State of Palestine. Palestinian culture is rich in traditions including Arabic language and literature, tatreez embroidery, dabke dancing, olive cultivation, traditional cuisine, and strong family and community ties. Despite decades of conflict, displacement, and political division, Palestinians maintain a strong connection to their homeland and a distinct national identity. #palestine #israel #map #maps #fyp
